rules.title: Own SQL status immediately and preserve first-failure diagnostics through cleanup
rules.applicability: Every SQL statement and surrounding business/error branch, across all categories.
rules.behavior: Record operation, SQLCODE, SQLSTATE/SQLWARN where relevant, row validity, expected no-row meaning, cardinality and next action. Observed targets use 0/100/OTHER, no named negative-code branches, no SQLWARN/SQLSTATE/affected-row checks. +100 means expected end for FETCH and absent restart row; missing required parent/event/business UPDATE/checkpoint UPDATE is rejected. SQLCODE 0 may still carry warnings or a multirow searched UPDATE. Do not invent implemented retry logic.
rules.minimum_storage: Immediate tests need no automatic saved-code helper. If SQLERROR executes rollback/logging/cleanup SQL before reporting the first failure, preserve original diagnostics in compatible existing/new storage only to that required lifetime. SQL-LOCATION must identify each operation, not a stale prior UPDATE.
rules.error_recovery: Verify SQLERROR/USERABEN termination and rollback; otherwise code can continue with invalid data, infinite cursor loop or false checkpoint. Distinguish constraint, duplicate, conversion/null, deadlock/timeout, authorization and ambiguous-commit scenarios when testing actual runtime; exact code/version policy is unprovided.
